parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, facility ban, border or custody exposure, police targeting, or state threat-framing is documented; discrimination and hate speech on gender identity are banned and courts have recognised hate motive and prosecuted a 2025 dating-app ambush case. That places the visitor well above unremedied universal-exposure regimes. Against that, equality bodies document rising violence and intimidation, especially affecting trans people, a recurring dating-app trap pattern with many incidents unreported from fear or shame, and a hate-crime recording gap that hampers prosecution under general provisions. Local gender-registration documentation conflict is a resident procedure open question, not a documented visitor document rejection. Combined, acceptance and legal protection are documented, but street/app violence and uneven recourse keep it below the consistently low-risk tier.

entry_documents.interaction: No documented border, passport-marker or ID-check friction for visitors; resident self-determination is only a climate signal.

investigation_detention_custody.interaction: No documented detention, placement, search or verification practice for trans visitors.

federal_state_facilities.interaction: No documented bathroom, ward or public-facility restriction at national or subnational level for visitors.

care_services.interaction: No documented visitor care, medication or emergency-treatment denial; resident conversion ban does not establish traveller care access.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Party politics described as a vector of hostility, but major-institution hostility largely absent; no trans offence or official threat framing documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Discrimination, hate crimes and hate speech on gender identity prohibited; hate motive recognised in court; conversion practices banned 2023.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Protective law coexists with no statutory hate-crime definition or recording code, so qualifying offences are prosecuted under general provisions.

minors_guardians.interaction: Resident minor marker route (parental consent plus psychological opinion at 16-17) does not govern a visiting minor's documents or care; no traveller-family rule documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Rising violence and intimidation reported, trans people especially affected; recurring dating-app traps lure victims to isolated ambush, robbery, humiliation or assault; many incidents unreported.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police have recorded incidents; May 2025 court case against three men accused of targeting at least eight victims; earlier hate-motivated murder conviction shows motive can be recognised.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A solo visitor using dating apps faces the documented trap pattern; fear/shame underreporting and lack of hate-crime recording weaken the documented prosecutions as a complete remedy.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Capital-region registration page still lists a medical certificate, possibly plus judicial/administrative decision, conflicting with national self-declaration; which local document set applies is unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National justice department states applications continue under self-determination pending replacement provisions after partial annulment in 2019.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: This is a resident-procedure conflict and open question, not documented rejection of foreign passports; custody, facility and care practices for visitors remain undocumented.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower: 0.35-A has a state-imposed universal birth-sex bathroom rule with courts rejecting complaints and no exemption. This dossier documents no such universal facility, border or custody rule and no state targeting, only street/app violence with prosecutions.

Similar but slightly higher: 0.65-A has lawful expression, accepted passports, convictions for attacks, but uneven police and slow complaints. Here protections are broader and present, yet a recurring dating-app trap pattern, rising reported violence and hate-crime recording gaps prevent a higher score.

Higher: 0.85-A documents broad acceptance, identity-based facilities, prompt regulator compensation, police conviction and medication access, with only occasional friction. This dossier lacks documented visitor-facing service enforcement for facilities/care and documents a patterned ambush risk and underreporting, so it sits below 0.85.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is protective in law and official framing, with no documented traveller-facing universal exclusion or organised state targeting, and courts/police have acted in hate-motivated cases. The operative risk if outed or targeted is therefore mainly societal and situational: rising intimidation and a recurring dating-app ambush pattern, many cases unreported, compounded by no hate-crime definition or recording code. Unknowns on custody, facilities and care are not documented exposures and were not treated as safety, but they also do not out-vote the documented legal protections. Resident self-determination and family law were used only as climate signals, per the rubric.
